sections.title: The letter í
paragraphs: The letter is called (í) /iː/. It makes only one sound. You hear this sound in the word (íz) /ˈiːz/, which means taste. This sound is a vowel, which means you make it with open air and no touch in the mouth. It is always a long vowel, so you hold it longer.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Spread your lips wide into a smile. Push your tongue high and far forward in your mouth. Keep the air flowing smoothly through the small gap at the top. Turn your voice on and hold the sound steadily. Place a hand on your throat. You will feel your vocal cords shake through the whole sound.

sections.title: When to use it
paragraphs: This letter always marks the long vowel sound in every position. You find it at the start, in the middle or at the end of a word. The accent mark shows that you must hold the sound for more time. You hear it in the word (híd) /hiːd/, and also in the word (tíz) /tiːz/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not shorten this sound into the quick vowel of bit. Do not glide your tongue into a diphthong, like the vowel sound in see. Keep your tongue high and completely still from start to finish. Hold the vowel twice as long as the vowel in beet, without moving your lips or jaw.
